summary: Top-performing videos by views consistently achieved a stayed_pct above 50%, whereas the bottom third experienced erratic or collapsed retention (falling as low as 16.2% despite a 100% anomaly on a single-view video).
High-stayed videos utilize punchy, direct statements in the first sentence that create an immediate cognitive gap or challenge a common assumption, avoiding filler or meta-introductions.
Titles of top videos incorporate high-contrast phrasing and relevant emojis to anchor the topic visually, contrasting with lower-performing titles that rely on generic questions.
Successful hooks rely on declarative sentences stating a counterintuitive fact ('Fresh pineapple is literally eating you back') rather than conversational throat-clearing.
Optimal duration for high-traction videos clusters around 17 to 38 seconds, while longer formats (over 50 seconds) severely risk early drop-offs.
winning_hooks: Your fingers prune in water, but it is not because you are absorbing it like a sponge.
Your eyes are leaking right now, and your brain is hiding it.
Fresh pineapple is literally eating you back.
This shark is older than the United States.
avoid: Starting hooks with conversational questions like 'Have you ever noticed...' or 'Did you know...'
Using lengthy descriptive setups that fail to deliver a core paradox within the first 5 words
Exceeding 45 seconds on niche explanatory topics where the initial premise does not immediately hook the scroll
next_experiment: Test two variations of a new hook: Variant A uses a direct counterintuitive statement ('Your kitchen sponge is dirtier than your toilet'), while Variant B uses a direct question ('Is your kitchen sponge dirtier than your toilet?'), tracking stayed_pct to see which drives a higher initial retention rate past the 3-second mark.
